newsitem.title: USA: Analysts welcome Northeast Utilities move.
newsitem.headline: Analysts welcome Northeast Utilities move.

text.p: Connecticut's Northeast Utilities took a major step Wednesday towards putting its troubled nuclear operation back on track, company officials and Wall Street analysts said.

But whether the move will speed up the reopening of Northeast Utilities' three main nuclear power plants, closed for months because of safety concerns raised by the federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), remains to be seen.

Bruce Kenyon, president and chief executive officer of the utility's nuclear division, said earlier Wednesday three borrowed utility executives - all with experience at companies with excellent operations - would direct the recovery of Northeast Utilities' three Millstone nuclear plants.
"We need individuals who have strong credibility with the regulators and others," Kenyon said.
He also said in a speech to employees that the company was abandoning the centralization of its nuclear units in order to improve accountability.
He named Admiral David Goebel as vice president for nuclear oversight.

John Cowan, a vice president at Carolina Power & Light Co, will lead the recovery effort at the Millstone 3 plant; Martin Bowling of Virginia Power, a subsidiary of Dominion Resources will help with Millstone 2's recovery and John McElwain of PECO Energy, will do the same for Millstone 1.
The Millstone facility in Waterford, Conn., produces some 2,700 megawatts of power when operating at full capacity.
"I believe this is an excellent move on the part of the company," said Daniele Seitz, vice president at UBS Securities.
The new managers were proven performers who likely had the NRC's blessing, she said.
"The anticipation that these people are going to take charge is a really big plus."
However, Seitz added that the changes would not necessarily speed up the plant reopenings, which most analysts say are unlikely this year.
"Estimates of the re-starts will probably be much more realistic than what we have heard in the past," she said.
The new managers "had nothing to lose" and would likely take their time to do a thorough overhaul, she said.
Two other Wall Street analysts said the changes were positive but not a surprise, because drastic action was called for.
A Northeast Utilities spokesman said the company was "very optimistic" about the changes but that a recovery timetable was still unclear.
"We hope it will make it faster, (but) we still don't have a schedule yet," Tony Castagno, manager of nuclear communications at Northeast Utilities, told Reuters.
Castagno said repair work on the Millstone 3 plant was expected to be finished by the end of this autumn.
Northeast Utilities closed 1/8 higher Wednesday at 12-1/2.
-- Matthew Lewis, New York newsroom + 1 212 859 1639
